result.title: Learning How to Search for Plans with Exponentially Less Space
result.summary: Heuristic search for a plan can store exponentially many states, even when its heuristic is almost perfect. We instead learn search control, one specification per domain, written as an indexical policy: a generalized policy with registers that hold objects and modes that sequence its rules. We add the choose rule, which loads an object into a register and marks a backtracking point, where one candidate suffices; every other rule must work for all of its outcomes and needs no search. Our main result is that structural termination, which rules out infinite executions, also bounds every execution by a polynomial in the number of objects. A depth-first procedure then finds a plan in polynomial space, however large the state space, with no list of visited states. The cost is time, exponential only in the choice depth, the number of real choices along an execution. Any class that such a policy solves therefore lies in NP, and in P at constant choice depth. We learn these policies with a language model in a counterexample-guided loop that certifies termination, verifies the training tasks, and keeps the choice depth small. With the learned policies, the procedure solves 1,709 of 1,890 test tasks of the IPC 2023 Learning Track and the Autoscale Agile suite, more than LAMA, BFWS, and Levitron, and most of them within one second and 100 MiB.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为规划问题学习「索引式策略」（带寄存器与模式、并新增 choose 规则的广义策略），证明结构终止可把每次执行限制为对象数的多项式，从而用深度优先回溯在多项式空间内求解，并用语言模型在反例引导循环中学习策略，在 IPC 2023 与 Autoscale Agile 上超过 LAMA 等基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「choice depth」限制的深度优先回溯与学习到的搜索控制策略，可能与 LVR 中控制推理循环、停止决策及动态计算预算的刻画存在概念联系，可供核查；本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态。
